answer: What if a ballot had to seep through karst, not pour? Each identity drips one sediment layer per tide through slow rock, and after twelve tides of deposits it reaches the delta where a willow drinks. Conduit farms die by the fast-water check: dye in a sinking stream surfaces 4 km away in 10 hours, so ballots arriving through one channel in one tide burn together, bonds slashed. Forging 10,000 ballots needs 120,000 tide-layers plus $30 bonded per ballot, $300,000 locked. A willow drinks slow water; a flood all at once is a burst pipe, and burst pipes get capped — $30 gone per ballot.
